h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, י״ז Ki Seitzei, 17
The Third Meal and the Holiness of Eating

p: we say the zemiros of the holy Arizal
and apparently so the Arizal instituted it.
of the Friday night meal we say:
"I shall arrange for the meal," etc.,
"and I invite at it now," etc.;
for we invite the holiness to the meal.
there is no mention in the song
of any invitation to the meal;
that the holy Arizal instituted it
And one may give the reason:
at the meals of Friday night and the morning
for which the Sages did not institute
he therefore instituted that it be said
did they not institute at this meal
according to what is said in the Abudraham
as the reason for the different texts
it is known that on Shabbos
there is then the union of the Holy One, Blessed is He,
for Shabbos is the aspect of the bride, the queen;
and therefore at night we say
referring to the joy of the wedding;
And the distinction in the holiness of the meals
like the holiness of the prayers
and as has been explained many times.
And we find that the Sages instituted
the blessing of betrothal at the time of betrothal,
and the blessing of grooms at the time of marriage
and for this reason they instituted
corresponding to the blessing of betrothal,
and in the morning they too instituted Kiddush,
corresponding to the blessing of marriage.
אֵין אוֹמְרִים שׁוּם בְּרָכָה עַל הַכּוֹס
no blessing is said over the cup
except "Who creates the fruit of the vine,"
which is a blessing of enjoyment
it says in the holy Zohar
from which the bride is blessed;
and you say that they are seven?
is the one that sustains all," etc.;
the first blessing of the seven
is the secret of wine," etc.
And therefore they instituted Kiddush over wine,
to recite only "Who creates the fruit of the vine,"
Not so at the time of union:
אָז אֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם בְּרָכָה עַל הַכּוֹס
then there is no blessing over a cup at all.
the holy Arizal did not institute
that the song of the third meal be said
for at this meal one merits
to behold the radiance of Ze'eir Anpin,
"as though they were eating and drinking";
and in the holy Zohar (end of Parshas Mishpatim, II 126a):
in terms of eating and drinking,
as it says: "and they ate and drank";
which is like song over wine,
since it is as though they drank wine.
And the time when one merits
to behold the radiance of Ze'eir Anpin
is at the time of the meal,
בְּכָל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי
"In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned
I will come to you and bless you."
eating on Shabbos is like eating of the altar,
for on Shabbos every one of Yisrael
and "I will come to you and bless you."
And then at this meal, that of Ze'eir Anpin,
to behold the radiance of Ze'eir Anpin.
Therefore it is fitting to say the song
for it is the aspect of song over wine,
since it is like actual eating and drinking,

p: "Just as bread that is bought with tithe money,
so too 'water' that is bought with tithe money;
and it calls it water," etc.
Now this needs to be understood:
Perhaps it speaks of ordinary bread!
"and I will remove illness from your midst";
(in Yerushalmi Shabbos 14:3 and Vayikra Rabbah, parsha 16):
"'And Hashem will remove from you all sickness' (Devarim 7:15)
whose beginning is sweet and whose end is bitter";
for it is the root of the sicknesses,
And so they expounded (Bava Kamma 92b; Bava Metzia 107b):
And this follows what they said
and the anger of the gall";
and anger is the root of all sins,
all kinds of Gehinnom have power over him"
"and I will remove illness from your midst,"
that is, He will remove the yetzer hara
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית יא, ב)
and this is in the manner of what they said (Taanis 11b):
"as though the Holy One dwells within his innards,
and should not bring on the yetzer hara
as it says (in the Sifrei on Eikev)
against the Holy One, Blessed is He,
and it brings this from several pesukim;
"and I will remove illness from your midst,"
And this is the inference in the Gemara:
"Just as bread bought with tithe money";
for regarding eating the tithe it is written (Devarim 14:23):
וְאָכַלְתָּ שָׁם לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְגוֹ׳
"And you shall eat there before Hashem your God," etc.,
"so that you may learn to fear
For once he has come to Yerushalayim
he is like one eating before Hashem,
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, Blessed is He,
so that it not bring him
under the dominion of the yetzer hara;
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב שָׁם)
similar to what is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 154b)
the food that the Kohanim would partake of,
there was blessed every bit of food
so that there not accuse them
the eating of the Showbread for the Kohanim,
so the eating of the tithe helped
all the food they eat be blessed,
And this is what it says:
"And He will bless your bread and your water,"
that is, bought with tithe money;
"and I will remove illness from your midst,"
and this is through the blessing that it says:
"I will come to you and bless you,"
for they eat the tithe before Hashem.
And this is the meaning in the Gemara
for wine is the aspect of Gevurah,

p: And this is the matter of
what they said in the Gemara (Eruvin 65a):
and to pay reward to the wicked," etc.
Now as for why they did not say
that it was created for libations,
that it follows the reading of the Gemara
"Wine was not created in the world," etc.,
there is the wine of a mitzvah
and likewise what Rav Nachman said
But according to what has been said, it is well:
"And He will bless your bread and your water,"
for wine of a mitzvah, of blessing,
and the Gemara there does not speak of this.
is like eating of the altar,
and also every one of Yisrael
Did they not eat before Moshe?
at which a talmid chacham is present
is as though he enjoyed the radiance of the Shechinah";
"And He will bless your bread and your water,
and I will remove illness from your midst."
And the eating of Shabbos helps
even on weekdays, be in holiness,
the dominion of the yetzer hara;
"and I will remove illness from your midst,"
and through the eating of Shabbos
